topic: Emergency department waits across eight hospitals
decision: which emergency department should get funding for 12 extra triage nurses

columns.median_wait_min: median minutes from arrival to first seen by a doctor
columns.p90_wait_min: 90th percentile of the same wait, minutes
columns.left_without_being_seen_pct: percentage of visits that left before being seen
columns.ambulance_arrivals_pct: percentage of visits arriving by ambulance
columns.wait_clock_starts_at: event that starts the wait clock

findings.text: Central is the busiest department, with 14,822 visits in the quarter.
Non-urgent patients wait longest everywhere, as expected: a median of 106 minutes across the eight hospitals.
Riverside has the longest median wait for urgent patients: 58 minutes, about twice the 28-minute average of the other seven hospitals.
Eastfield has the highest share of ambulance arrivals (38%).
The slowest 10% of semi-urgent patients waited over three hours at 2 hospitals (Riverside, Northgate).

Northgate starts its wait clock at registration rather than at triage, which adds about 15 minutes. Its 41-minute urgent wait is about 26 minutes on the same basis as the other hospitals, so it is not really the second-slowest.
Westbrook has the fewest staffed beds (18).
Riverside also has the most patients leaving without being seen: 9.2% of visits, against an average of 3.2% at the other hospitals.
Visits across the network were up 4% on the previous quarter.
Lakeview has the shortest waits in every triage category.

main.gist: Riverside has by far the longest urgent waits (and most patients leaving)

caveat.gist: Northgate measures waits from registration, so it is not comparable

facts.q: Which hospital has the longest median wait for urgent patients, and how many minutes is that wait?
